title: Introduce contextual sampling scheduler CI adapter for shot/context robustness
author: Anya Patel
description:
Motivation: Flaky CI failures and subtle regression signals often originate from a small fraction of contexts (e.g., specific system prompts, turn counts, or few-shot exemplars). Current smoke/eval pipelines sample uniformly across prompts and shot counts which dilutes sensitivity to context-specific regressions. This PR introduces a Contextual Sampling Scheduler CI adapter that (1) collects shot/context distribution fingerprints for a prompt-set, (2) computes semantic clusters of contexts using a lightweight embedding + locality clustering, and (3) schedules prioritized, interleaved re-runs for clusters that historically produce higher variance. The adapter is designed to be a soft gate: it surfaces prioritized failures and can optionally escalate to CI-level hard-fail when a severity threshold is exceeded.

Summary of changes: single-string description that includes implementation, tests, and rollout notes. Added a new ci-adapters/contextual_sampling_scheduler module, a scheduler shim for existing smoke and regression jobs, a metric exporter for per-cluster variance/time series, and a small local CLI to visualize cluster stability. New config knobs: sample_budget, cluster_seed, severity_threshold, max_reruns_per_cluster. The scheduler integrates with Prometheus metrics and the existing eval-harness webhook to tag flaky samples for triage.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1987) 
- [x] Unit tests for scheduler heuristics (deterministic seed) 
- [x] Integration test that runs a small prompt-set with mocked model responses and verifies prioritized rerun ordering 
- [x] Metrics and dashboards (Grafana tile added) 
- [x] Backwards-compatible default config (adapter disabled by default)

Why this is safe: Defaults keep the adapter disabled; enabling requires explicit CI config opt-in per pipeline. The scheduling algorithm is deterministic when cluster_seed is set to avoid non-reproducible CI flakiness. We fall back to uniform sampling if embedding service is unavailable. No model invocation changes are made; the adapter only chooses which samples to re-run and in what order.

Testing & rollout: Unit tests added and pass in CI. Integration tests initially failed due to a race in the mock embedding client (see CI logs) — fixed by serializing cluster creation in tests. Rollout plan: opt-in on canary pipelines for 2 weeks, inspect cluster variance telemetry, then enable as soft gate on nightly regression runs before considering as a hard gate for PR CI.

review_comments: Marco Liu: Nice design. Two questions: (1) can you elaborate on failure modes when the embedding service is rate-limited? (2) do we risk doubling cost if we rerun many clusters?

Anya Patel: For (1) the adapter falls back to a cheap token-overlap heuristic and samples uniformly across clusters. For (2) there is a sample_budget config; default is conservative (10% extra runs). Both points are now documented in docs/ci-adapters/contextual-scheduler.md
Priya Desai: Integration test flaked on CI — looks like a timing issue in mock_embedding. Can you add a deterministic seed?
Anya Patel: Added cluster_seed and serialized setup in the latest commit (c2d3e11). Re-ran CI and integration tests became stable.
Rafael Gomez: Request: expose per-cluster historical variance in the API so SRE can alert on clusters with growing variance over time.
Anya Patel: Added prometheus metric eval_context_cluster_variance{cluster_id} and updated dashboard fragment to include historical timeseries.
